name: Pro-Tec Systems
what_they_do: Engineered fire alarm, security and low-voltage systems contractor for commercial, industrial, educational, institutional and multi-family residential buildings across central NJ, southern NY and eastern PA, in business since 1988. Sells service contracts or time-and-materials work, with in-house support staff and warehoused parts.
customers: Commercial, industrial, school/institutional and multi-family property owners and facility managers; a PO Box in Somerset handles mail.

size_signals.signal: Operating since 1988 with field technicians plus in-house support staff and a central parts warehouse
Separate sales and support mailboxes listed (sales@, support@, info@)
Coverage stated as NJ, southern NY and eastern PA

listing.reviews: review count not shown; listing is unclaimed and has no photos

website_review.trust_signals: Since 1988, service contracts, vendor logos (Siemens, Telecor, Faraday, Lathem)
website_review.out_of_date_signs: Site is a Microsoft FrontPage 5.0 build on the 'breeze' theme with table layout and gif buttons; page title is just 'Home' with no meta description; footer says Copyright 2008 and Last modified 03/25/08; an 'Under Construction' graphic is still live; the Feedback page form posts to FrontPage's _derived/nortbots.htm so it cannot actually deliver; the footer mailto points at protecsystems.org instead of .net; dozens of injected 'prada/gucci/instagram followers' spam links are hidden on every page, which points to the site being compromised and used as a link farm (inference)
website_review.search_basics: The visible text does name fire alarm/security services and the three-state service area, but there are no service-specific pages beyond a contents page, no town targeting, no meta description and no structured data; robots.txt returns a 404
top_issues: HTTPS certificate fails (ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID), so Chrome warns visitors off and some tools cannot load the site at all
Site is compromised with hidden injected spam links - a reputation and search-spam risk
Contact form is broken and the footer email address is a different domain
No mobile layout (no viewport meta, 1990s table design)
Google Business Profile unclaimed with the wrong category ('General contractor') and no hours or photos

agent_readiness.notes: There is a Google listing but it is unclaimed, categorised as a general contractor, with no hours and no photos - so it is barely a signal. robots.txt is a 404 (no blocking, but no sitemap either). Crawlable prose does describe services and territory, but there is no JSON-LD, no published hours, no price or contract detail, and the only form is non-functional.

operations_signals.signal: Support runs on generic mailboxes (info@/support@) with no ticket system or portal
Service contracts and T&M work imply recurring dispatch, scheduling and renewal admin

top_opportunities.opportunity: Emergency site rescue: restore a valid SSL certificate and strip the injected spam link farm
top_opportunities.evidence: Chrome reports a certificate name mismatch, and every page hides dozens of unrelated link-farm anchors

top_opportunities.opportunity: Claim and complete the Google Business Profile (hours, categories, service area, photos of installs)
top_opportunities.evidence: Maps shows 'Claim this business', category 'General contractor', no hours, no photos

top_opportunities.opportunity: Replace the dead FrontPage form with a working quote/service-request form plus one page per customer segment
top_opportunities.evidence: Feedback form posts to _derived/nortbots.htm; all segments share one paragraph on the home page

scores.reasons: A 35-year-old commercial contractor with real revenue and a badly broken digital front door; the highest-value fixes (cert, spam cleanup, GBP claim) are small jobs that a solo consultant can deliver in days.

wrong_claims.claim: HTTPS certificate fails with ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID (name mismatch)
wrong_claims.what_is_true: The certificate does fail, but with an incomplete chain ('unable to get local issuer certificate'), not a name mismatch; the hostname on the cert is fine, the intermediate issuer is missing.

wrong_claims.claim: dozens of injected spam links are hidden on every page
wrong_claims.what_is_true: The injected prada/gucci/'instagram followers'/chatgpt anchors are rendered visibly - 16px inline links with non-zero bounding boxes on the home and feedback pages (119 anchors on the home page) - not hidden. The compromise and link-farm risk still stands, and it is arguably worse because visitors see it.
